open_points.subject: owner-only listener topology
open_points.text:
Registry is one process (R0-05) serving two surfaces (Actors and trust
boundaries, "Network surface"): the service API, for the four services of A09,
and the owner interface. Which networks reach each surface, and the HTTPS that
carries the owner interface from another machine, are the host's
administration (R0-28, R0-29, R0-48; Explicit exclusions): Registry serves
each surface it opens — the service API not at all in an owner-only start
(A17 rule 1) — on a listener of its own, at its configured address, and
decides nothing about reachability beyond that listener's own form — bound
exclusively, an IPv6 one for IPv6 alone (A17 rule 1).
open_points.question: Does the statement that Registry serves two surfaces describe only the full-start capability, with an owner-only start serving one surface, or does it require every running process to serve both surfaces?
options: Registry has two possible surfaces, but an owner-only start serves only the owner interface.
Every running Registry serves both surfaces, including an owner-only start.
open_points.default_guess: Treat "serving two surfaces" as describing the full-start capability and open only the owner-interface listener in an owner-only start.

witness.initial: The configuration contains the owner-interface settings and none of the four service tokens or the service-API address, so A17 permits an owner-only start.
events: The owner starts Registry with that configuration.
Registry completes its configuration checks and begins serving.
outcomes: The process opens only the owner-interface listener because the service API is "not at all" served in an owner-only start.
The process must nevertheless expose both listeners because it is stated to be "serving two surfaces".
witness.observer: A service client or host administrator checking whether a service-API listener exists.
